correctness.rationale: Affine normalize a centered three-zonotope to generators (1,0),(0,1),(p,q), p,q>0. Independently reconstruct the six vertices, six polar support vertices, and unnormalized tensor moments from exact polygon determinant formulas: their trace product reproduces 8N/(9D) for x,y,z pairwise absolute generator determinants. The algebraic upper gap 75D-64N expands at x=W+U+V,y=W+U,z=W to exactly 46 positive integer monomials, including 1024 W^7(U^2+UV+V^2): it vanishes only at U=V=0. The lower gap factors as 8pq H(p,q)/(9(1+p)^3(p+q)^3(1+q)^3), with all 19 coefficients of H positive, and tends to 0 as one positive generator shrinks. At p=q=1 the exact moment gives 25/24; limiting parallelograms have 8/9. Hence no extrapolation from finite tests is required.
residual_risks: The theorem requires six genuine vertices and center-based polarity; degeneration supplies only the unattained lower endpoint.
The determinant parametrization is for centered 3-zonotopes in the plane and cannot be extrapolated to general nonsymmetric six-gons.

value.rationale: The quadratic Ball–Santaló polar moment is a classical affine invariant. Determining its *sharp* global range, unique affinely regular optimizer, and nonattained parallelogram boundary in the complete natural centrally symmetric six-gon moduli gives a nontrivial structural polygon extremal theorem. The 46-monomial certificate is materially stronger than quoting the general ellipsoid inequality; its exact constant is not a routine substitution.
residual_risks: No implication for asymmetric hexagons or more sides.
